title: Marshall Islands Adopt Self-Government Constitution
description: On 1 May 1979 the Marshall Islands ratified a republican constitution and inaugurated Amata Kabua as first President, formally separating from the US-administered Trust Territory of the Pacific Islands. The new state retained close defence and economic ties with Washington pending a Compact.

title: Compact of Free Association Approved by Plebiscite
description: Marshallese voters approved the proposed Compact of Free Association with the United States by a wide margin in a UN-observed plebiscite. The vote authorised the framework that would govern defence, migration and economic assistance for decades.

title: Compact of Free Association With United States Enters Force
description: The Compact of Free Association came into force in October 1986, granting full sovereignty while reserving US defence rights, free entry for Marshallese workers and 15 years of economic assistance. The Compact also created a Nuclear Claims Tribunal for testing-era victims.

title: Trust Territory of the Pacific Islands Effectively Terminated
description: With the Compact in force, the United Nations Trusteeship over the Marshall Islands effectively ended, though formal termination at the UN waited until 1990. The Marshall Islands began conducting an independent foreign policy alongside Compact obligations.

title: Nuclear Claims Tribunal Established
description: The Nuclear Claims Tribunal began hearings to compensate victims of US nuclear testing conducted at Bikini and Enewetak between 1946 and 1958. The tribunal awarded billions in damages over its lifetime although most claims went unpaid.

title: Marshall Islands Admitted to the United Nations
description: The Marshall Islands joined the United Nations on 17 September 1990 following formal termination of the US trusteeship. Membership cemented international recognition of full sovereignty.

title: Reagan Test Site Lease Renewed at Kwajalein
description: The US Army's missile-testing facility at Kwajalein Atoll, the Ronald Reagan Ballistic Missile Defense Test Site, secured continued land-use rights from displaced Marshallese landowners. Lease payments became a major income source for affected families.

title: Amata Kabua Dies in Office
description: Founding President Amata Kabua died on 19 December 1996 after 17 years leading the republic. His cousin Imata Kabua was elected by parliament to succeed him.

title: Diplomatic Recognition Switched to Taiwan
description: The Marshall Islands transferred diplomatic recognition from Beijing to Taipei, becoming one of Taiwan's small but loyal Pacific allies. The relationship has produced steady aid flows and high-level visits.

title: Kessai Note Becomes First Commoner President
description: Senator Kessai Note was elected by parliament in January 2000, becoming the first Marshallese president from outside the traditional iroij chiefly class. His victory marked a generational shift in national politics.

title: Compact of Free Association Amended
description: The Marshall Islands and the United States signed an amended Compact extending grant funding for another 20 years and creating a Compact Trust Fund intended to provide income after 2023. Shipping registry, postal and telecommunications cooperation were also reaffirmed.

title: Litokwa Tomeing Elected President in Power Shift
description: Senator Litokwa Tomeing's coalition unseated Kessai Note's faction, the first peaceful change of governing coalition since independence. The new government emphasised compact-fund accountability and a more independent diplomatic stance.

title: Tomeing Removed by No-Confidence Vote
description: Parliament removed President Tomeing on a no-confidence motion in October 2009 amid disputes over Compact spending. Senator Jurelang Zedkaia was elected to serve out the term, demonstrating parliamentary checks on executive power.

title: Christopher Loeak Wins Presidency
description: Iroij Christopher Loeak was elected president in January 2012, ushering in a focus on climate diplomacy and the Majuro Declaration on Climate Leadership. His term elevated Marshallese voices in regional Pacific diplomacy.

title: Majuro Declaration on Climate Leadership Adopted
description: Pacific leaders meeting in Majuro signed a declaration calling for an immediate ramp-up of global climate ambition, branded the 'Pacific Wave'. The declaration positioned the Marshall Islands as a moral leader of the High Ambition Coalition.

title: Marshall Islands Sues Nuclear Powers at ICJ
description: The Marshall Islands filed cases at the International Court of Justice against the nine nuclear-armed states for failing to negotiate disarmament under the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty. The audacious litigation drew global attention before being dismissed on jurisdictional grounds in 2016.

title: Major King-Tide Floods Hit Majuro
description: Severe inundation events in early 2014 swamped homes, the airport runway and the cemetery in the capital Majuro, displacing hundreds. The floods became a focal point for Loeak's climate-leadership messaging.

title: Marshall Islands Pivotal in Paris Agreement
description: Foreign Minister Tony de Brum led the High Ambition Coalition that secured the 1.5 degree Celsius aspiration in the Paris Agreement. The Marshall Islands became symbolic of the climate vulnerability narrative throughout the COP21 process.

title: Hilda Heine Becomes First Female President
description: Senator Hilda Heine was elected in January 2016 as the first female president of any Micronesian state and the first elected female head of an independent Pacific Islands country. Her victory followed a successful no-confidence motion against Casten Nemra.

title: Sovereign Cryptocurrency Law Passed
description: Parliament passed the Sovereign Currency Act creating SOV, an officially recognised cryptocurrency intended to operate alongside the US dollar. The IMF warned the move risked banking-correspondent-relationship loss and the project was repeatedly delayed.

title: Heine Survives No-Confidence Vote on SOV Crypto
description: President Hilda Heine narrowly survived a no-confidence motion in November 2018 brought by senators opposed to the SOV cryptocurrency project. The 16-16 tie preserved her government but exposed deep parliamentary divisions.

title: David Kabua Elected President
description: Senator David Kabua, son of founding president Amata Kabua, was elected by parliament in January 2020. The transition continued the Marshallese tradition of competitive but consensual presidential selection.

title: COVID-19 Border Closure
description: The Marshall Islands imposed strict border closures and remained one of the world's last COVID-free jurisdictions for nearly two years. Compact-related travel from the US became sharply restricted, isolating diaspora communities.

title: First Major COVID-19 Outbreak
description: Community transmission of COVID-19 was confirmed in Majuro and Ebeye in August 2022 after years of zero cases. The outbreak strained the limited health system and caused dozens of deaths.

title: Hilda Heine Returns to Presidency
description: Hilda Heine was elected president for a second time in January 2024 by the new parliament after the November 2023 general election. Her platform emphasised renegotiating Compact terms and accelerating climate adaptation.

title: Compact of Free Association Renegotiation Agreed
description: The Marshall Islands and the United States agreed in October 2023 on a renewed 20-year Compact funding package worth roughly USD 2.3 billion, including a dedicated trust fund for nuclear legacy issues. US Congressional appropriation was secured in March 2024.

title: Marshall Islands Submits Sovereign Climate Plan
description: President Kabua's government delivered the Marshall Islands' Survival Plan, a long-term framework for raising or relocating populated atolls in response to projected sea-level rise. The plan attracted international donor support.

title: Compact Funding Disbursed
description: The first tranches of the renewed Compact funding flowed to Majuro after US Congressional appropriation, restoring fiscal stability and enabling delayed infrastructure projects. The Compact Trust Fund received a substantial supplementary contribution.

title: China Coast Guard Incident Near Marshallese EEZ
description: A reported close-pass incident between a Chinese maritime vessel and a Marshallese-flagged ship heightened concerns about strategic competition in the Northern Pacific. The Heine government reaffirmed defence cooperation with Washington and Taipei recognition.

title: Bikini Cleanup and Compensation Talks Resume
description: Renewed bilateral talks reopened the question of US responsibility for nuclear-test contamination at Bikini and Enewetak, with Marshallese leaders demanding a permanent settlement of unpaid Nuclear Claims Tribunal awards. The renegotiated Compact carved out a separate bilateral track for legacy claims.
